rows.question: How can I change the HTTP port the embedded server listens on?
rows.baseline_answer:
Set the `server.port` property. Spring Boot's `ServerProperties` binds it, and the embedded container (Tomcat, Jetty, Undertow, Netty) picks it up.

**application.properties**
```properties
server.port=9090
```

**application.yml**
```yaml
server:
  port: 9090
```

Other ways to set the same property:

- **Command line:** `java -jar app.jar --server.port=9090`
- **Env var:** `SERVER_PORT=9090`
- **JVM system property:** `-Dserver.port=9090`

Notes:

- `server.port=0` makes the server bind a random free port. You can read the actual port at runtime by injecting `@LocalServerPort` (test scope) or via `WebServerApplicationContext.getWebServer().getPort()`. For a servlet app under `@SpringBootTest(webEnvironment = RANDOM_PORT)`, `@LocalServerPort` resolves it.
- For programmatic control, register a `WebServerFactoryCustomizer<ConfigurableServletWebServerFactory>` (or the reactive equivalent) and call `factory.setPort(...)`.
- The property prefix is `server.port` for the standard single-connection setup. If you're using additional connectors (e.g. a second Tomcat connector via `TomcatConnectorCustomizer`), those are configured separately.
- `management.server.port` is the equivalent for the Actuator endpoints if you want them on a different port.
rows.rag_answer: Set it with the `server.port` property (for example, in `application.properties` or as a System property). You can also use `SERVER_PORT` as an OS environment variable. To switch off the HTTP endpoints completely, use `server.port=-1`.

rows.question: How do I exclude a specific auto-configuration class from being applied?
rows.baseline_answer:
Use the `exclude` attribute on `@SpringBootApplication` (or `@EnableAutoConfiguration`):

```java
@SpringBootApplication(exclude = DataSourceAutoConfiguration.class)
public class MyApplication {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        SpringApplication.run(MyApplication.class, args);
    }
}
```

If the class may not be on the classpath, use `excludeName` with the fully qualified class name instead:

```java
@SpringBootApplication(excludeName = "org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.jdbc.DataSourceAutoConfiguration")
```

Or exclude it via configuration property — `application.properties`:

```properties
spring.autoconfigure.exclude=org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.jdbc.DataSourceAutoConfiguration
```

`application.yml`:

```yaml
spring:
  autoconfigure:
    exclude:
      - org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.jdbc.DataSourceAutoConfiguration
```

- Both `spring.autoconfigure.exclude` and the annotation attributes work; if you set both, the annotation and property are effectively combined (the property is also useful for tests via `@SpringBootTest(properties = ...)`).

rows.question: How do I enable detailed health information in the Actuator health endpoint?
rows.baseline_answer:
Set the following property:

```properties
management.endpoint.health.show-details=always
```

Other accepted values:

- `never` — default; no details shown to anyone
- `when-authorized` — details shown only to authenticated users with the roles listed in `management.endpoint.health.roles`
- `always` — details shown to all callers

If you use `when-authorized`, specify the allowed roles, e.g.:

```properties
management.endpoint.health.show-details=when-authorized
management.endpoint.health.roles=ADMIN
```

Optionally, to include per-component details (each `HealthIndicator` individually):

```properties
management.endpoint.health.show-components=always
```

Note that `show-components` governs component visibility while `show-details` governs the details inside each component; the effective visibility is the narrower of the two, so with `show-details=always` and `show-components=never` you still get aggregate details.

Also make sure the endpoint is exposed:

```properties
management.endpoints.web.exposure.include=health
```

(Or include it in your existing list.) The result is visible at `/actuator/health`.

How much detail you get also depends on each `HealthIndicator` — e.g. `management.info.env.enabled` and the `management.health.*.enabled` flags control which indicators contribute at all.

rows.question: Which Actuator endpoint exposes application metrics?
rows.baseline_answer:
**`/actuator/metrics`** — it exposes the metrics collected by Micrometer.

Notes:

- It must be exposed. By default, only `health` is exposed over HTTP (WebFlux/WebMvc), so you typically need:
  ```properties
  management.endpoints.web.exposure.include=health,metrics
  ```
  (In Spring Boot 3.x, `health` is the only one enabled/exposed by default; all others must be explicitly exposed.)
- You can list all metric names with `GET /actuator/metrics`, and inspect a specific one with `GET /actuator/metrics/{name}`, e.g. `/actuator/metrics/jvm.memory.used`. Tag filtering is done via query params, e.g. `/actuator/metrics/http.server.requests?tag=status:200`.
- If you need a Prometheus-scrapeable format, add the `micrometer-registry-prometheus` dependency, which exposes **`/actuator/prometheus`** instead (often used alongside `/actuator/metrics`).

Property names to double-check in your version: the exposure include property is `management.endpoints.web.exposure.include`; the base path is `management.endpoints.web.base-path` (default `/actuator`).

rows.question: How do I configure the JDBC connection URL for the default data source?
rows.baseline_answer:
Set `spring.datasource.url` in your configuration. For example, in `application.properties`:

```properties
spring.datasource.url=jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/mydb
spring.datasource.username=myuser
spring.datasource.password=mypass
```

Or in `application.yml`:

```yaml
spring:
  datasource:
    url: jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/mydb
    username: myuser
    password: mypass
```

Notes:

- `spring.datasource.url` is the canonical property name. (The older `spring.datasource.jdbc-url` is **not** read by auto-configuration for the default data source — it's used in some manual/`DataSourceProperties`-based setups.)
- Spring Boot auto-configures a `DataSource` bean from these properties; the driver is inferred from the URL, so `spring.datasource.driver-class-name` is usually optional (set it if you have multiple drivers on the classpath).
- If you're using an embedded database (H2, HSQLDB, Derby) on the classpath, Spring Boot creates an in-memory datasource automatically without any URL — your `spring.datasource.url` overrides that.
- Spring Boot 2.x+ uses HikariCP by default; connection-pool tuning goes under `spring.datasource.hikari.*`.
- For multiple data sources, auto-configuration doesn't apply the same way —

rows.question: How do I configure which Actuator endpoints are exposed over HTTP?
rows.baseline_answer:
Use the `management.endpoints.web.exposure.*` properties.

```properties
# Expose only these two over HTTP
management.endpoints.web.exposure.include=health,info

# Expose everything
management.endpoints.web.exposure.include=*

# Exclude specific ones (takes precedence over include)
management.endpoints.web.exposure.exclude=threaddump,heapdump
```

Key points:
